p: שַׁבָּת יֵשׁ בּוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא כָּל הַיּוֹם כַּיָּדוּעַ,
— Shabbat contains the revelation of Atika throughout the day, as is known.
וּבְרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ אִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ עט ב) אוּף הָכִי בְּחַדְתּוּתֵי סִיהֲרָא דְּהָא נָהִיר לָהּ שִׁמְשָׁא בְּחֶדְוָותָא דִּנְהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא לְעֵילָא.
— Concerning Rosh Chodesh, the Zohar (III, 79b) teaches: “So too, when the moon is renewed, the sun illuminates her with the joy of the radiance of Atika above.”
וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק לוּרְיָא זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה כָּתַב שֶׁמּוֹפִיעַ רַק בְּעֵת מוּסָף וְלָכֵן אוֹמְרִים קְדוּשַּׁת כֶּתֶר וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִסְתַּלֵּק.
— The Ari, of blessed memory, writes that this radiance appears only during Musaf, which is why we recite the Kedushah beginning “Keter”; afterward it departs.
וְכֵן בַּחֲנוּכָּה שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר אֵל הַשֵּׁם וַיָּאֶר לָנוּ עַל חֲנוּכָּה וְעַל כֵּן אוֹמְרִים בּוֹ אֶת הַהַלֵּל (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם פָּרָשָׁה ב׳),
— The same applies to Chanukah: the Pesikta interprets “Hashem is God, and He has given us light” as referring to Chanukah, and therefore we recite Hallel then (as stated there, section 2).

וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁאָז מִתְגַּלֶּה מֵאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל יְדֵי הַנֵּרוֹת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַדְלִיק שֶׁמְּקַיֵּים מִצְוַת זְקֵנִים וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה וַיָּאֶר לָנוּ בָּאוֹר הַנִּגְנָז לַעֲמֵלֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא (וְנִתְבָּאֵר חֲנוּכָּה מַאֲמָר ב׳),

— We have explained that the primordial light is then revealed through the lamps Hashem lights, fulfilling the commandment of the elders. Through this, “He has given us light,” with the light hidden for those who labor in the Oral Torah, from the dew of Atika (as explained in Chanukah, discourse 2).

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 79b (Achrei Mot 74:408–409): “Rabbi Shimon said: It is written, “From new moon to new moon and from Shabbat to Shabbat.” Why are these equated? They all ascend to one level, and one unites with the other. Their joy in one another is found only when the Holy Ancient One is revealed; then there is joy for all. We learned: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day”—for the Shabbat day itself; it is praise with which the Holy One, blessed be He, is praised. Then joy is found and an additional soul is granted, for the Ancient One is revealed and union is prepared. So too, when the moon is renewed: the sun illuminates her with the joy of the radiance of the Ancient One above. Therefore this offering is directed above, so that everything may be sweetened and joy may be found in the world. Hence, “Bring an atonement offering for Me”—the wording is exact.”

paragraphs.text: Sha’ar HaKavanot, Derushei Rosh Chodesh, paragraph 3: “This explains why we say “A crown they shall give You” in the Rosh Chodesh Musaf, as on Shabbat. There is, however, a difference: on Rosh Chodesh we do not say “From His place may He turn in compassion to His people” or “His glory fills the world,” as on Shabbat and festivals. The reason is that the Keter spoken of on Shabbat reflects the ascent of Zeir Anpin and his feminine counterpart to the actual Keter of Father and Mother. We therefore say “Where is the place of His glory?” and “From His place may He turn,” praying that although they have ascended to that exalted place, He should not forget us, but turn toward us in compassion. On Rosh Chodesh, however, the Keter spoken of concerns the ascent of the feminine counterpart only to the Keter of Zeir Anpin. Therefore “Where is the place…” does not apply, for Ayyeh refers to Father and Mother and the supernal Daas—the three upper sefirot of Father and Mother.”

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbati §2, opening passage: “Why do we kindle lamps on Chanukah? When the sons of the Hasmonean high priest defeated the Greek kingdom, as it says, “I will arouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece,” they entered the Temple and found eight iron spits. They fixed them in place and kindled lamps in them. Why do we recite Hallel? Because it is written, “The Lord is God, and He has given us light.” Why do we not recite it on Purim? It is written, “To destroy, kill, and annihilate” their enemies, but Hallel is recited only over the fall of a kingdom, and Ahasuerus’s kingdom remained. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, brought the Greek kingdom to an end, they began offering hymns and praise, saying: “Formerly we were servants of Pharaoh, servants of Greece; now we are servants of the Holy One, blessed be He: Praise, servants of the Lord!””

p: רַק הַהֶבְדֵּל הוּא אֵיךְ שֶׁבָּא הַהַמְשָׁכָה.
— The distinction lies only in the manner in which this spiritual flow descends.
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת הַהַמְשָׁכָה עַל יְדֵי קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא הַנָּהָר הַיּוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן.
— On Shabbat the flow comes through the middle line, through Jacob’s aspect, the river issuing from Eden.
וְיַעֲקֹב בְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכוֹן וְגוֹמֵר דְּאָחִיד לְהַאי וְכוּלֵי לְעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ קעה ב),
— Jacob is “the middle bar,” and so forth, “which grasps this,” and so forth, “the holy Atika” (as stated in Zohar II, 175b).
וְעֵדֶן עִלָּאָה כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּקּוּן נה),
— The higher Eden is the supernal Keter (as stated in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 55).
וְיַעֲקֹב הַנָּהָר הַיּוֹצֵא תִּפְאֶרֶת וְהַהַמְשָׁכָה עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף דְּהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת יְסוֹד.
— Jacob, the river issuing forth, is Tiferet, and the flow is conveyed through Joseph’s aspect, the chariot for the attribute of Yesod.

לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן דָּא שְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה וְהַמְשָׁכָה זוֹ דַּוְקָא עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא נָהָר דְּנָגִיד וְנָפִיק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קצו ב וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת),
— “To water the garden”—the lower Shekhinah. This flow comes specifically through Joseph, “the river that flows and issues forth,” as stated in the holy Zohar on this portion (196b and elsewhere).
וְהַהַמְשָׁכָה עַל יְדֵי בְחִינָתוֹ.
— The flow is conveyed through his aspect.
וּבְרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא רַק הוּא עַל יְדֵי סִיהֲרָא דִּמְקַבְּלָא מִשִּׁמְשָׁא דְּנָהִיר לָהּ מִנְּהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא.
— On Rosh Chodesh there is also a revelation of Atika, but through the moon receiving from the sun, which illuminates her with Atika’s radiance.
וּבַחֲנוּכָּה הַהַמְשָׁכָה עַל יְדֵי קַו הַשְּׂמָאלִי מִבִּינָה שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל עֵדֶן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ כו א),
— On Chanukah the flow comes through the left line, from Binah, which is also included in Eden (as stated in Zohar I, 26a),
וּמִדַּת גְּבוּרָה וְהוֹד דַּרְגָּא דְּאַהֲרֹן שֶׁקְּדוּשַּׁת נֵר חֲנוּכָּה בָּא עַל יְדֵי כֹּהֲנֶיךָ הַקְּדוֹשִׁים.
— and the attributes of Gevurah and Hod, Aharon’s level, for the sanctity of the Chanukah lamp comes through “Your holy priests.”

h: The Missing Alef Among the Tribes

p: וּבָזֶה יֵשׁ לוֹמַר מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים כּוּלָּנוּ בְּנֵי אִישׁ אֶחָד נַחְנוּ כֵּנִים אֲנַחְנוּ וְגוֹמֵר,
— This explains the tribes’ words, “We are all sons of one man; we are honest,” and so forth, using first nachnu and then anachnu for “we.”
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (ר א) נַחְנוּ אֲנַחְנוּ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ אַמַּאי חָסֵר א׳ בְּגִין דְּרָזָא דִבְרִית לָא אִשְׁתְּכַח עִמְּהוֹן אִסְתַּלַּק מִתַּמָּן א׳ וְכוּלֵי,
— The holy Zohar (200a) asks: “‘Nachnu’—it should say ‘anachnu.’ Why is the alef missing? Because the mystery of the covenant was not present with them, the alef departed from there,” and so forth.
וּלְבָתַר אָמְרוּ כֵּנִים אֲנַחְנוּ אִתּוֹסַף א׳ אָמְרוּ וְלָא יָדְעוּ מַה קָאָמְרוּ וְכוּלֵי,
— “Afterward they said, ‘We are honest,’ using anachnu, with the alef added. They spoke without knowing what they were saying,” and so forth.
מְנָלָן דִּכְתִיב וַיֹּאמְרוּ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר עַבְדְּךָ אַחִים אֲנַחְנוּ וְיוֹסֵף אִיהוּ בְחוּשְׁבָּנָא כַּד אָעֵל בְּחוּשְׁבָּנָא אָמְרוּ אֲנַחְנוּ וְכַד לָא אָעֵל בְּחוּשְׁבָּנָא אָמְרוּ נַחְנוּ.

— “How do we know? It is written, ‘They said: Your servants are twelve brothers,’ and Joseph is included in the count. When he entered the count, they said anachnu; when he did not enter the count, they said nachnu.”
וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין בִּשְׁלָמָא אַחַר כָּךְ אָמְרוּ אֲנַחְנוּ שֶׁבְּמִסְפָּר י״ב נִכְלָל גַּם יוֹסֵף,
— We must understand this: their later use of anachnu is understandable, since Joseph was included in the number twelve.
וּמִקּוֹדֶם כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ כּוּלָּנוּ בְּנֵי אִישׁ אֶחָד נַחְנוּ שֶׁנִּתְכַּוְּונוּ עַל עַצְמָם שֶׁהָיוּ רַק עֲשָׂרָה אָמְרוּ נַחְנוּ בְּלֹא א׳.
— Earlier, when they said, “We are all sons of one man,” referring to themselves, only ten brothers, they used nachnu without the alef.
אֲבָל לָמָּה אָמְרוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ דִיבּוּר כֵּנִים אֲנַחְנוּ דְּקָאֵי גַּם כֵּן עַל עַצְמָם שֶׁנֶּחְשְׁדוּ לִמְרַגְּלִים.
— But why did they say in that same speech, “We are honest,” using anachnu, when this too referred to themselves, who were suspected of being spies?

p: וּלְפִי הָאָמוּר יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּאוֹת א׳ מְרַמֵּז לִנְהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא פֶּלֶא עֶלְיוֹן.
— According to the foregoing, the letter alef alludes to the radiance of Atika, the supernal wonder, pele, whose letters are those of alef.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב׳ נד א) כַּד אִתְנְהִיר נְהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא וְכוּלֵי נְהִירוּ דְּאָלֶף וְכוּלֵי,
— As stated in the holy Zohar (II, 54a): “When the radiance of the holy Atika shines,” and so forth, “the radiance of the alef,” and so forth.

וְהַהַמְשָׁכָה מִנְּהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא עַל יְדֵי קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי וּבְחִינַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַנָּהָר דְּנָגִיד וְכוּלֵי.

— The flow from Atika’s radiance through the middle line, the aspect of Jacob our father, peace be upon him, is possible only through the attribute of the righteous one, foundation of the world, the aspect of the river that flows, and so forth.

וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ כּוּלָּנוּ בְּנֵי אִישׁ אֶחָד שֶׁהִזְכִּירוּ קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לָכֵן כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין יוֹסֵף נִכְלָל עִמָּהֶם אָמְרוּ נַחְנוּ דְּאִסְתַּלַּק אָלֶף מִתַּמָּן.
— Thus, in saying “We are all sons of one man,” they invoked Jacob’s sanctity. Since Joseph was not included with them, they said nachnu, for the alef had departed from there.
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר הַהַמְשָׁכָה עַל יְדֵי קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי בְּלֹא יוֹסֵף.
— For the flow through the middle line is impossible without Joseph.

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ כֵּנִים אֲנַחְנוּ בְּאָלֶף שֶׁמִּצִּדָּם שֶׁהֵם כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכִין לְהֶאָרַת נְהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא שֶׁהוּא אָלֶף וְהוּא כְּעֵין הִתְגַּלּוּת נְהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ גַּם כֵּן דֶּרֶךְ קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי רַק דְּנָהִיר לָהּ שִׁמְשָׁא וְכוּלֵי,

— Nevertheless, they said “We are honest,” anachnu with an alef: as the Community of Israel they attain the illumination of Atika’s radiance, signified by alef. This resembles Atika’s revelation on Rosh Chodesh, which also does not follow the middle line, but comes when “the sun illuminates her,” and so forth.

וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר עַבְדֶּיךָ אַחִים אֲנַחְנוּ שֶׁבְּמִסְפָּר י״ב נִכְלָל גַּם יוֹסֵף לָכֵן אַף שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנֵי אִישׁ אֶחָד וְגוֹמֵר שֶׁהוּא קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ בְּאָלֶף אֲנַחְנוּ כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּלְלוּ לְיוֹסֵף בַּמִּסְפָּר.

— Later, when they said, “Your servants are twelve brothers,” including Joseph among the twelve, even though they also said “sons of one man,” invoking Jacob’s sanctity, they nevertheless used anachnu with the alef, since they included Joseph in the count.

וְכֵיוָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף נָהָר דְּנָגִיד וְנָפִיק יוּכְלוּ לִזְכּוֹת לִנְהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא הַהַמְשָׁכָה מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן דֶּרֶךְ קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּכוֹן וּכְמוֹ הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דְּשַׁבָּת.

— With Joseph’s aspect present, the river that flows and issues forth, they can attain Atika’s radiance: the flow from the supernal Keter along the middle line, through the sanctity of Jacob our father, the middle bar, like the revelation of Shabbat.

This is song, song from every side; this is “Then Moses sang.””

paragraphs.text: Connection: The two letters alef and zayin form az, “then.” The Zohar thus links the song at the sea to the radiance of Atika through the alef.

Through Joseph’s holiness one can merit Jacob’s holiness, the aspect of truth.”

h: Delight in the Three Shabbat Meals

p: וְשָׁלֹשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת שַׁבָּת בְּרָזָא דְּעוֹנֶג עֵדֶן נָהָר גַּן,
— The three Shabbat meals embody the mystery of oneg, delight: Eden, river, and garden, whose initials form that word.

וְזוֹכִין לְהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא עַל יְדֵי קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי דְּמוּסַף שַׁבָּת נֶחְשָׁב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (תּוֹלְדוֹת) כְּנֶגֶד מִדַּת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא הַנָּהָר דְּנָגִיד וְנָפִיק וְעַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עַמּוּדָא דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא יוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן עִלָּאָה כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן שְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה וְכָאָמוּר.

— They attain Atika’s revelation through the middle line. Shabbat Musaf is reckoned in the Zohar Chadash, Toldot, as corresponding to Joseph, the river that flows and issues forth; through Jacob’s sanctity, the middle pillar, it issues from the higher Eden, the supernal Keter, to water the garden, the lower Shekhinah, as explained.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beshalach 8:1: “Wherever there is a revelation of Atika there is no place for prayer and arousal from below, as we find, ‘One who delights in Shabbat is granted the desires of his heart.’ For oneg, delight, is the initials of Eden, nahar, gan, as stated in the holy Zohar (I, 26a). We have already said that although it says there, ‘Eden is the supernal Mother,’ when one merits the higher Shabbat, Eden includes all three first sefiros. … Just as the vav, the middle pillar, is the river issuing from the lower Eden, the upper Heh, to water the garden below, the lower Shechinah, so the yud, Chochmah, issues from the upper Eden, the supernal Keter, to water the garden, the upper Heh. … The alef signifies the supernal Keter, as in the holy Zohar, ‘The alef pierced through the darkness’: that is, alef as pele elyon, the supernal wonder.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Toldot 38–39: “Come and see: corresponding to those seven righteous ones, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded in the Torah that an additional offering be brought on seven occasions during the year, to add delights and pleasures for them from the King’s house, so that the fathers be satisfied first and then the children. These are seven occasions and no more. rich.text: Zohar Chadash, Toldot 38–39

: “Come and see: corresponding to those seven righteous ones, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded in the Torah that an additional offering be brought on seven occasions during the year, to add delights and pleasures for them from the King’s house, so that the fathers be satisfied first and then the children. These are seven occasions and no more. On Shabbat, it corresponds to the righteous one, foundation of the world, who is called “All” and is called Shabbat, to add delights for him from the concealed mind. On Rosh Chodesh, it corresponds to the Congregation of Israel, which is called the moon.”
